# LiFePO4 is the better choice for most people

**LiFePO4 (also called LFP or lithium iron phosphate)** is the better pick for nearly every buyer in 2026. **NMC** still makes sense only if you need the lightest possible unit and will use it rarely.

## How they compare

| | LiFePO4 (LFP) | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| **Rated cycle life** | Usually 3,000–6,000 cycles | Usually 500–1,000 cycles |
| **Weight** | Somewhat heavier | About 10–16% lighter in finished stations |
| **When a cell fails** | Burns cooler and slower | Hotter and more violent |
| **Price** | Mainstream, often cheaper per Wh | Mostly older or compact models |
| **Availability** | Standard in current models | Legacy and clearance stock |

### Cycle life: the biggest difference
- **LFP:** In one guide's database of current models, the median rating is 4,000 cycles for LFP versus 800 for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Daily use:** If you charge from solar every day, a 500-cycle NMC battery reaches its 80% capacity point in under 2 years. A 3,000-cycle LFP battery takes about 8 years ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Occasional use:** For a few outages or trips a year, either chemistry will age from time before it runs out of cycles.
- **Fine print:** Check the end point on the rating. "4,000 cycles to 70%" promises less than "4,000 cycles to 80%."

### Weight
NMC cells hold much more energy per pound. Much of that edge disappears in a finished station, because the inverter, case and fans weigh the same either way. One database found NMC stations only about 10% lighter per watt-hour ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Another found about 16% ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Some LFP models are actually lighter than older NMC ones ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).

### Safety
In lab studies, failing LFP cells reached much lower temperatures. Some only smoked, while NMC cells threw flames ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). That matters for a unit you keep indoors or in a vehicle.

LFP is **not fireproof**, though. The U.S. Department of Energy notes that LFP systems have had incidents too ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Be skeptical of claims that LFP "can't catch fire" or needs no ventilation, which one of the search results makes.

### Cold weather
This is mostly a tie. Nearly all stations of either chemistry won't charge below 32°F (0°C) ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Check the manual for the specific model rather than relying on the chemistry.

## Which should you buy?
- **Daily or frequent use** (van, RV, off-grid, solar): LiFePO4, with the highest cycle rating you can find.
- **Kept indoors for home backup:** LiFePO4.
- **Weight-critical and used rarely:** Compare specific models. A discounted NMC unit can be fine.
- **Already own a working NMC station:** Keep using it.

## A LiFePO4 example
**BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** ([buy at BLUETTI via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2), [details](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2))
- 2,073.6 Wh capacity, rated for 6,000+ cycles to 80%
- 2,600 W inverter and ≤15 ms UPS switchover
- 24.2 kg (about 53 lb), 5-year warranty
- Not expandable
- Price: $899, or $854.05 with code **AFF5OFF**. The site says the code worked in BLUETTI's cart on 2026-10-24, but the final price at checkout is what counts.
